data.description:
# Re-architect the DC transport along CAPABILITY seams, so it stops needing rescue splits

## Why now (operator-approved as a separate change)

`transport.py` is at **799/800**. The next parent-related change cannot land. This is the fourth
time in one day the file has forced prose-trimming to fit: 756 → 780 (1302) → 794 → 781 (1305) →
799 (1311 + 9bb9). Each rescue bought a few lines and none addressed why growth keeps landing here.

## The diagnosis: the previous splits were REACTIVE, so they did not change where code goes

Two extractions already happened, both under cap pressure, both along whatever seam was nearest:

    retry.py        258 LOC   retry policy + error translation   (story S1 of b586)
    transitions.py  166 LOC   transition resolution + routing
    transport.py    799 LOC   EVERYTHING ELSE

`transport.py` re-exports the extracted names as a facade, so from a caller's view nothing moved.
Critically, **neither split gave a NEW operation an obvious home**. A new capability still has
exactly one plausible destination — the god file — so the file re-grows to the cap and the cycle
repeats. b586's own lesson (S1 mechanical relocation passed plan review FIRST TRY where the combined
ticket took ten rounds) was about splitting *a change*; it did not fix the module's shape.

## The insight: the right seam ALREADY EXISTS and is not being used

`_backend.py` defines the capability Protocols this class implements — `TicketTransport`,
`SupportsLinks`, `SupportsComments`, `SupportsAbsenceProbe`. Those ARE the module's natural
boundaries, and the class already satisfies them. The file is organised by nothing; the contract is
organised by capability. Aligning the two means every future operation has a determined home:
*"which capability is this?"* answers *"which file does it go in?"*

## Proposed architecture — capability mixins composed by a thin transport

Reading the current method inventory, the clusters are clean and already disjoint:

    _base.py        ~120   shared plumbing: __init__, _client, _unwrap, _call_logged,
                           _user_attr, _paged_search  (the mixins' common substrate)
    _issues.py      ~180   create_issue, get_issue, get_issue_by_rest, update_issue,
                           delete_issue, search_issues
    _hierarchy.py   ~150   set_parent, _resolve_epic_link_field_id, get_parent_map
                           <- where 39c1 / 9bb9 / future parent work LANDS
    _links.py       ~120   set_relationship, get_issue_links, get_issuelinks_map,
                           delete_issue_link
    _comments.py    ~100   add_comment, get_comments, get_comment_map
    _people.py      ~130   _assign, set_reporter, validate_assignee_exists
    _properties.py  ~110   _put_property, set_issue_property, set_entity_property
    transport.py    ~150   the composition root: class JiraDataCenterTransport(...mixins),
                           build_client_from_settings, _jira_client_class, __all__ facade
    (retry.py, transitions.py unchanged)

Every unit lands in the **200–500 target band or just under**, and none is a sub-100-LOC fragment —
the two failure modes the module-size policy names.

**`JiraDataCenterTransport` remains ONE class**, composed from mixins, so `isinstance` against the
Protocols, `assert_transport_conforms`, and every caller and test keep working with no edit. That is
what makes this a *mechanical relocation* rather than a redesign — and, per b586's evidence, what
makes it reviewable in one pass.

## Why mixins rather than delegation or free functions

Delegation (`self._issues.create_issue(...)`) would change the call shape at every site and break
Protocol conformance. Free functions taking a client would lose the shared cache (`_epic_link_field_id`)
and the `_call_logged` wrapper. Mixins keep one object, one cache, one `self`, and move only the
*text*. The cost is that mypy needs the shared attributes declared on a base — hence `_base.py`
rather than bare mixins.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] behaviour is UNCHANGED: this is a relocation. No test assertion is edited, and the full
      `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` suite (2105 at time of filing) passes untouched
- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport` remains a single class satisfying the same Protocols —
      `assert_transport_conforms` and the shape contract `tests/_jira_shape_contract.py` pass unedited
- [ ] the `transport.<name>` facade still resolves for every currently re-exported name, so
      `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` and friends pass UNEDITED (the reason `__all__` exists)
- [ ] every resulting module is between 100 and 500 LOC; none exceeds the 800 cap
- [ ] `_resolve_epic_link_field_id` has exactly ONE definition after the move — the duplication
      9bb9 deliberately avoided must not be reintroduced by the split
- [ ] a short note in the package docstring states the organising principle (one module per
      capability Protocol) so the NEXT operation has a determined home rather than defaulting here
- [ ] done as its own change, landing BEFORE further parent work, per the operator's approval

## Explicitly out of scope

Changing any behaviour, touching `retry.py`/`transitions.py`, or altering the Protocols themselves.
data.title: Re-architect the DC transport along capability seams to stop chronic cap-driven splits
